papers.title: FedDES: Graph-Based Dynamic Ensemble Selection for Personalized Federated Learning
papers.publication_status: versioned arXiv preprint; independent peer-reviewed body equivalence unverified
papers.operation: Independently fitted/exchanged heterogeneous classifiers; decision-profile sample graph plus classifier nodes, class-aware reference neighbors, local correctness-gain edges; heterogeneous GATv2 meta-learner trained on per-classifier correctness BCE; sigmoid>0.5 selection and normalized hard-prediction voting, uniform fallback.
limitations: Graphs encode sample decision-profile similarity and sample-classifier competence, not a shared live task-GNN backbone or original observed graph transport.
The local TRAIN role is used both to fit local base classifiers and supervise meta-learning; honest out-of-fit competence for an own selected shared backbone is not specified.
Gain subtraction is a common per-query offset; top-k gain ranking equals weighted local correctness ranking. This does not establish equality of later normalized-edge/meta-GNN behavior.
Printed gain normalization is not resolved for zero/nonpositive gain cases; author implementation was not read.
No paper quality, publication equivalence, source reproduction or federated-to-WikiCS transfer is certified.

papers.title: PREF-Gate: Provenance-Constrained Relational Evidence Fusion with Validation-Gated Selection for Graph Fraud Detection
papers.publication_status: versioned arXiv preprint; independent peer-reviewed body equivalence unverified
papers.operation: Separate histogram-gradient-boosting label-free context expert and Extra-Trees evidence expert; one-hop attribute mean/residual/degree, self-excluded TRAIN neighbor risk, leave-one-out prevalence and empirical-Bayes support/variance summaries; five fixed validation candidates select one global expert/mixture and threshold.
limitations: No query-dependent neural gate or shared capable GNN backbone; validation selects one candidate globally for the split.
The source deduplicates/symmetrizes edges and inserts self-loops; this is not the current all-nonself-record attention normalization or preserved multiplicity.
Its per-node self-exclusion and leave-one-out prevalence do not directly prescribe common whole-Q exclusion from all derived fields in the current recipe.
Global concentration is estimated from supported TRAIN nodes; porting to a stronger all-Q context contract needs an explicit masked-context versus fitted-parameter treatment.
Selected threat-to-validity paragraph discloses post-development revision; no independent replication or reported gains are transferred.
The finite coefficient candidate set is source ancestry, not a new coefficient grid proposal.

reusable_findings: Node/classifier competence selection is established dynamic ensemble stacking; a classifier-sample meta-graph is not the original task relation graph.
Shared learned receiver conditioning, graph filters, sender/receiver communication and query-dependent attention are prior; current query-key attention already conditions scores on the target.
TRAIN-label-only context and label-free relational context have different support domains; receiver feature modulation cannot activate a zero label field.
Learned competence can be in-sample if the same TRAIN role fits bases; honest fusion/meta labels require reservation before native fitting and checkpoint selection.
A common per-query baseline subtraction does not change member ranking; code must resolve normalized signed/zero gains before transferring an implementation.
Empirical-Bayes global statistics need explicit treatment under any stronger common-Q exclusion rule; do not conflate self-exclusion with whole-Q masking.
